chain.title: A Bent Stick
chain.desc: Five sticks in a hook. Hit leaves with it and they give up saplings far more readily than a bare hand, plus the occasional silk worm.

chain.title: The First Hammer
chain.desc: Planks and sticks. It smashes cobblestone into gravel, gravel into sand, sand into dust, and that descending line is the whole economy of a skyblock.

chain.title: Barrel
chain.desc: Planks around a slab. Fill it with leaves or saplings and wait and you get dirt; fill it with water and lava and you get stone. Free matter from nothing.

chain.title: Silk Worm
chain.desc: Shaken out of leaves by the crook. Put one back on a leaf block and it slowly infests it, and infested leaves break into string.

chain.title: Cooked Silk Worm
chain.desc: A silk worm in a furnace. Genuinely edible, and in the opening hour of a skyblock that is not nothing.

chain.title: Stone Hammer
chain.desc: The second rung. Same job as the wooden one but it survives long enough to be worth carrying, and the ladder continues up through netherite.

chain.title: Sieve
chain.desc: Planks, a slab and sticks. The other half of the mod: everything the hammer breaks down goes through here to be picked over for seeds and ore.

chain.title: String Mesh
chain.desc: Six string in a frame. A sieve does nothing without a mesh, and this coarsest one is what gets you your first saplings and seeds.

chain.title: Pebbles
chain.desc: Sifted out of dirt and gravel four at a time. Four pebbles make a cobblestone, which is how a world with no stone in it gets stone.

chain.title: Dust
chain.desc: Sand hammered one step finer. Sifted, it gives the bone meal, redstone and glowstone that no amount of gravel will ever produce.

chain.title: Flint Mesh
chain.desc: String mesh reinforced with flint. Second rung of the mesh ladder, and the first one that will let ore chunks through at all.

chain.title: Wooden Crucible
chain.desc: A log and a slab. Drop leaves and saplings in and it renders them slowly into water, which a world without an ocean badly needs.

chain.title: Porcelain Clay
chain.desc: Clay and bone meal kneaded together. Ordinary clay cannot survive a crucible full of lava; this can.

chain.title: Unfired Crucible
chain.desc: Seven porcelain clay in a bowl shape. Fragile and useless until it has been through a furnace, like every real piece of pottery.

chain.title: Porcelain Crucible
chain.desc: The unfired crucible smelted. Now it will hold cobblestone and turn it into lava, which is the single biggest jump in the mod's power curve.

chain.title: Iron Mesh
chain.desc: Flint mesh bound with iron. Third rung, and the one that opens the sieve up to the middle band of the ore chunk table.

chain.title: Ore Chunks
chain.desc: Sifted out of gravel and crushed rock. Smelt it like raw ore; this is where a world with no stone finally starts producing metal.

chain.title: Golden Mesh
chain.desc: Iron mesh gilded. Fourth rung. The returns per sieve pull rise with every rung, which is the only reason to keep climbing.

chain.title: Diamond Mesh
chain.desc: Golden mesh set with diamonds. Fifth rung, and the point at which sifting stops being a chore and starts being a factory input.

chain.title: Netherite Mesh
chain.desc: Diamond mesh through a smithing table with a netherite ingot and an upgrade template. Top of the mesh ladder and the best drop table in the mod.

chain.title: Compressed Blocks
chain.desc: Nine dirt in a square. The compressed forms exist so the compressed sieve and hammer can process nine blocks in one action instead of one.

chain.title: Compressed Sieve
chain.desc: A log, iron and sticks. Takes compressed blocks and returns nine blocks' worth of drops per pull, which is the first real throughput upgrade.

chain.title: Mechanical Sieve
chain.desc: An iron block, a hopper, glass and iron bars. Runs on Forge Energy and sifts without you, which is where the mod hands off to the tech mods.

chain.title: Mechanical Hammer
chain.desc: An iron block, a hopper, iron and a hammer to seat inside it. Powered crushing; between the two machines the whole loop automates.

chain.title: Grass Seeds
chain.desc: Sifted from dirt. Scatter them on a dirt block and it becomes grass, which is what lets animals spawn and the world stop being sterile.

chain.title: Witch Water
chain.desc: Mixed in a barrel from water, mushrooms and gunpowder. Drop mobs and blocks into it and they turn into their darker counterparts.

chain.title: End Cake
chain.desc: Crushed end stone, eggs, sugar and an eye of ender. Eat a slice and it moves you to the End, which for a skyblock is the only door there is.

chain.title: Sculk Core
chain.desc: An echo shard and an ender pearl. A late curiosity that gives the deep dark's materials to a world that never had a deep dark.

notes: Verified against exdeorum-1.53.jar from Modrinth project 'ex-deorum'; META-INF/mods.toml gives modLoader='javafml', modId='exdeorum', version='1.53', minecraft versionRange='[1.20.1]' and forge versionRange='[47,)' - a native 1.20.1 Forge build with no other hard dependencies. ID COUNT: 236 item models, 165 blockstates, 75 item.exdeorum.* and 166 block.exdeorum.* lang keys. The union across all four is 242; five of those are lang-only and are NOT items, so the registered count is 237. LANG-ONLY PHANTOMS dropped (the inverted-convention failure mode): 'infested_leaves.fully_infested' (a state suffix appended to the block name), 'mechanical_hammer.hammer_label' and 'mechanical_sieve.mesh_label' (GUI labels reading 'Hammer:' and 'Mesh:'), 'random_armor_trim.no_upgrade' (a tooltip line) and 'watering_can_fluid_display' whose value is literally ': %s / %s' - a format string, not a name. A naive item.<modid>.* sweep turns all five into ids. Also dropped: 'oak_barrel_composting', a blockstate with no lang key and no item model, which is the render-only state of a barrel mid-compost. THE BIG STRUCTURAL FACT - MOST OF THE JAR IS CONDITIONAL WOOD VARIANTS. Of the 229 exdeorum ids produced by some recipe, 88 sit behind a forge:mod_loaded condition: 40 on 'biomesoplenty' (fir, hellbark, jacaranda, magic, mahogany, palm, redwood, umbran, willow, dead barrels/sieves/crucibles/compressed sieves), 32 on 'blue_skies' (bluebright, comet, crystallized, dusk, frostbright, lunar, maple, starlit), 10 on 'ars_nouveau' (the blue/green/purple/red archwood set, whose lang names are Cascading, Flourishing, Vexing and Blazing Archwood) and 6 on 'aether' (skyroot). NONE of those were used anywhere in this file - every wood-variant wheel above is restricted to the 141 unconditional outputs, which is vanilla woods plus stone. If the pack ships BoP or Blue Skies those families become legal additions; if it does not, quoting them would be an uncompletable quest. RECIPE TYPES: exdeorum:sieve (539) and exdeorum:compressed_sieve (539) dominate, wrapped in 729 forge:conditional envelopes; then crafting_shaped (97), barrel_compost (63), hammer (26), water_crucible (26), tag_result (15), crucible_heat_source (11), barrel_mixing (8), compressed_hammer (8), barrel_fluid_mixing (5), crook (4). NOTE ON EXTRACTION METHOD: the forge:conditional wrapper means a top-level 'result' key scan finds nothing - the real recipe is nested inside conditional.recipes[].recipe. An unwrapped scan reported 0 outputs for this mod; unwrapping it produced 229. Anyone re-deriving this set must recurse. THE TWO LADDERS are the backbone and both are real dependency chains, not cosmetic tiers. Mesh: string_mesh (string only) -> flint_mesh (consumes string_mesh) -> iron_mesh (consumes flint_mesh) -> golden_mesh (consumes iron_mesh) -> diamond_mesh (consumes golden_mesh) -> netherite_mesh (consumes diamond_mesh plus minecraft:netherite_upgrade_smithing_template). Hammer: wooden -> stone -> iron -> golden -> diamond, each an independent craft from rods plus its material, then netherite_hammer which consumes diamond_hammer and the smithing template. The netherite rung of both ladders needs the vanilla template, so both are gated behind a bastion. OBTAINABILITY - KEPT DESPITE NO CRAFTING RECIPE: exdeorum:silk_worm is produced by the four exdeorum:crook recipes (crook used on leaves), not by a bench. exdeorum:porcelain_bucket has a smelting recipe from unfired_porcelain_bucket and is in a wheel. exdeorum:witch_water_bucket needs a word of explanation because an automated obtainability check flags it: the BUCKET ITEM has no recipe of its own, but the FLUID it holds has an explicit one - data/exdeorum/recipes/barrel_fluid_transformation/witch_water.json turns a barrel of minecraft:water into exdeorum:witch_water with red and brown mushrooms as weighted byproducts. The fluid is also registered into data/minecraft/tags/fluids/water.json alongside exdeorum:flowing_witch_water, and two further recipes consume it (barrel_fluid_mixing/netherrack.json and barrel_mixing/soul_sand.json), so the fluid is unambiguously live. Filling a vanilla bucket from a registered fluid that ships a bucket item always works, so the step is completable; the quest text should say 'fill a bucket from a barrel of witch water' rather than implying a craft. This is a stricter standard than was applied to the Ender IO fluid buckets, which were dropped - there the FLUIDS themselves had no verified recipe, only machine output, whereas here the fluid's recipe is in the jar. DROPPED FOR NO VERIFIED SOURCE: 'exdeorum:infested_leaves' - it has a blockstate, an item model and a lang key, but no recipe and no loot table; it is placed by using a silk worm on a leaf block, which is code-registered, so it is very likely reachable but nothing in the data proves it and it was left off rather than guessed. The four filled porcelain buckets (porcelain_lava_bucket, porcelain_milk_bucket, porcelain_water_bucket, porcelain_witch_water_bucket) were likewise dropped - they are fill-by-use variants of the empty bucket with no recipe of their own. 'exdeorum:witch_water' (the fluid block) dropped as a fluid registration rather than an item. DESIRABILITY: the jar carries a large number of _slab, _stairs and _wall variants of the compressed and crushed blocks; per the rule none appear in the chain, and the wheels use only the base blocks. 'exdeorum:random_armor_trim' is kept in a wheel despite its _trim suffix - it is not a block trim variant but a genuine sieve reward item with its own model, lang key and two sieve recipes (data/exdeorum/recipes/sieve/sand/golden/random_armor_trim.json). ORDERING vs moddb consensus (15 entries, all 15 id-verified): NO SERIOUS CONFLICT, which is unusual. Consensus reads crook 0.0, oak_barrel 0.071, silk_worm 0.143, cooked_silk_worm 0.214, stone_hammer 0.286, oak_crucible 0.357, string_mesh 0.429, porcelain_clay_ball 0.5, dust 0.571, porcelain_crucible 0.643 and the recipe graph agrees with all of it. The only adjustment made was inserting exdeorum:wooden_hammer before stone_hammer (consensus omits it entirely, but it is the cheaper first rung and the crafting recipe is planks plus rods, strictly earlier than the stone one) and moving oak_sieve up beside string_mesh, since a mesh is inert without a sieve to seat it in.
